source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: Meta has significantly outpaced Google/Gemini in frontier model capability and deserves credit for returning to competitiveness from a position of weakness
summary_extended: Baker argues that Meta has executed a remarkable turnaround in frontier AI model capability, going from being effectively out of the competitive race roughly 12 months ago to now being significantly ahead of Google's Gemini in model capability — a shift he describes as 'unimaginable' just a year prior. He credits Meta's team with doing 'a great job' and frames this as a genuine competitive repositioning, not a marginal improvement. Baker also notes that Grok has emerged as a third credible frontier model alongside OpenAI and Anthropic, suggesting the frontier is not collapsing to a single winner. The investment implication is that Meta's AI capability trajectory is underappreciated relative to the prior narrative of Google dominance, and that GOOGL faces a more serious competitive threat in AI than the market may have priced in — while META deserves a re-rating as a credible frontier AI leader.
